text:
John Adams defending British soldiers after the Boston Massacre in 1770 is one of those acts where u really have to question, would u have had the stones to do that

five ppl killed, murder charges, no lawyer in the city would risk taking the case for the British defense

Adams agrees to do it driven by belief in rule of law and the right to a fair trial, and to establish that the colonies had a functional system that wouldn't bend to politics

city turns on him, Adams loses half his legal practice, but argues that the soldiers were acting in self-defense against a riotous mob

six soldiers get acquitted, two get a lesser charge, none hanged

months later, Adams gets elected to the house of representatives, and later reflects on the case as "...one of the most gallant, generous, manly and disinterested actions of my whole life, and one of the best pieces of service I ever rendered to my country."

does the wise man make that choice, idk, there's a hundred ways it could have ended in disaster or death

but it was a high-risk bet that went in Adams' favor, and posterity now knows it as a defining act of courage...
